title: South-west Western Australian runoff at equal rain did not fall after the 1970s rain decline, but fell 25-45% from 2000-2001, 2-3 years after the south-east Australian drop (CAMELS-AUS, 1952-2021)
abstract: Question: after 1997, south-east Australian (SE-AU) runoff fell 12-25% below its rainfall-runoff relation and stayed low. Is this a climatic response to less cool-season rain, or a state shift that a drought starts? South-west Western Australia (SW-WA) gives an independent test: its May-October rain fell near 1969-1975, about 25 years before the SE-AU shift. Approach: CAMELS-AUS v2.03 flow and AGCD rain (SILO check), calendar years 1952-2021. Per catchment, sqrt(Q) = a + bP + cP(t-1) fitted on 1952-1974, with the same code for 11 SW-WA and 71 SE-AU catchments; window departure = observed/predicted flow - 1; bootstrap over catchments. The plan was written before any SW-WA efficiency result. Post hoc: a 1975-1996 reference (47 SW-WA, 230 SE-AU) and a reference-free step scan of 44 and 234 long records. Results: in 1975-1996 SW-WA rain was 7% below 1952-1974, but runoff was only -5.3% (95% interval -8.9 to +11.7%) below the relation. It then fell to -28% in 1997-2009 and -51% in 2010-2021 (all 11 catchments). The regional step was in 2001 (bootstrap 2001-2001), against 1999 (1998-1999) in SE-AU; the SW-WA rain step was in 1969. Relative to 1975-1996, SW-WA runoff fell 25% in 2001-2009 and 45% in 2010-2021 while rain fell only 4-6% further. In the reference-free scan, 64% of SW-WA records had a clear step down (permutation null 1.6%), median year 2000 (IQR 1998-2001); SE-AU 63%, median 1998. Six early steps (1979-1984) were all in catchments with at least 93% of native forest. Two SW-WA dry runs with equal rain deficit (-14%) and equal warmth (Tmax +0.44 and +0.48 C) differed: runoff was -1% in the 8 years after 1976-1980 but -47% after 2001-2007. Conclusion: the SW-WA rain-regime decline did not start the loss in most catchments for about 25 years. In both regions efficiency fell within a few years around 1997-2001, after droughts that were not deeper or warmer than earlier droughts that left no loss. The open question becomes what changed in southern Australian catchments or droughts near 1997-2001. Limitations: few SW-WA records before 1975, in one forested area; land-use changes (clearing, logging, mining) not modelled; simple annual model; timing cannot separate a common trigger from region-specific droughts; many analyses are post hoc; data end in 2021.

display.caption: Runoff at equal rain relative to each catchment's 1952-1974 relation (top) and May-October rain anomaly (bottom) for SW-WA (11) and SE-AU (71). SW-WA rain fell from 1969, but its runoff efficiency fell only from 2001; SE-AU fell from 1999.

Reference-free step scan: year of the best downward step in runoff at equal rain for 44 SW-WA and 234 SE-AU long records, and a map of SW-WA step years. Early steps (1979-1984) are in fully forested catchments.
SW-WA runoff departures during and after two dry runs with equal rain deficit and warmth: the 1976-1980 run left no lasting loss; the 2001-2007 run left a loss of about 47%.

citations.reason: It pooled SW-WA into southern Australia; we test SW-WA timing against its own earlier rain shift.
Chile megadrought gave no deficit at equal rain; with SW-WA, a lower rain regime alone does not give the loss.
The WWII drought left no SE-AU loss; we find an equal SW-WA analogue (1976-1980 vs 2001-2007).
Found a 1997-1998 Victorian step; we find a SW-WA step in 2000-2001 with the same annual approach.
The 1997 step followed winter-rain share; SW-WA, the most winter-dominated region, stepped later, not at its rain shift.
Reported rain-sensitivity loss after 1997; our SW-WA form test depends on the transform, as it cautioned.
The 1997-1999 drop was not global; we find a second southern Australian region that dropped at nearly the same time.
Seven climate terms did not explain SE-AU efficiency; SW-WA timing adds a cross-region test of the rain-regime term.
Daily climate explained at most one third of SE-AU efficiency changes; our SW-WA dry-run comparison also finds no climate difference.
Found a persistent low state in Victoria; we find a similar persistent state in SW-WA from 2001.
CAMELS-AUS v2 flow, rain, Tmax and attributes (CC BY 4.0).
Linked SW-WA runoff ratio to groundwater storage; early steps in forested catchments agree with this.
HMM study of shifts in eastern and western Australia; we add the step timing relative to each region's rain shift.
Earlier analysis of multiyear drought and the annual rainfall-runoff relation in Australia.
